newsitem.title: USA: INSTANT VIEW - US Feb industrial output up 0.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - US Feb industrial output up 0.5 pct.

text.p: Following are comments from U.S. economists after the Federal Reserve reported that industrial production rose 0.5 percent in February while capacity utilization registered 83.3 pct.
In January industrial output fell by a revised 0.1 percent and capacity utilization came in at a revised 83.2 percent.
JAMES ANNABLE, CHIEF ECONOMIST, FIRST CHICAGO NBD: "This is one day that encapsulates the Fed's dilemma. This is strong growth in the economy and yet we don't have much sign of inflation."

CARY LEAHEY, SENIOR FINANCIAL MARKETS ECONOMIST, LEHMAN GOVERNMENT SECURITIES: "The numbers were a little softer than expected, but they still showed pretty good gains. We had a small increase in motor vehicles.

"What the market will like, and what's making a mild positive for the fixed-income markets anyway, is that the capicity utilization rate remains fairly subdued. So, it's a strong number, but the market knows these numbers are going to be strong."

CHERYL KATZ, SENIOR ECONOMIST, MERRILL LYNCH GOVERNMENT SECURITIES: "It doesn't look like there were any surprises here. Manufacturing we knew was strong from the employment report. You had a rebound in mining, which was to be expected. And utilities, given the better weather conditions in February, had gone down.
"One can characterize the manufacturing sector as gradually showing improvement. I believe there continues to be few bottlenecks at the manufacturing level, which is a good sign for inflation."
